title: AI for Data Analysis
description: Use AI to analyze spreadsheets, find patterns, create charts, and extract insights — without writing a single formula.

data.text: One of the most powerful and underused AI capabilities for non-technical professionals is data analysis. Upload a spreadsheet, describe what you want to know, and get instant analysis, charts, and insights — no formulas, no pivot tables, no coding. This lesson covers practical prompts, verification strategies, integration patterns, and advanced techniques to make AI-driven analysis reliable and repeatable.

data.text: What you can analyze with AI

rows: "Give me a summary: min, max, average, and count by region"
"Show monthly revenue for 12 months and highlight anomalies"
"Group customers by purchase frequency: 1, 2-5, and 6+ times"
"Is there a relationship between lead response time and close rate?"
"Which 10 products have the lowest profit margin? Sort lowest first."
"Find rows with missing values. Show me counts by column."
"Add a column: cost per acquisition = ad spend divided by new customers"
"What are the most common themes in the feedback column?"

cards.title: ChatGPT Plus (Code Interpreter)
cards.description: The most capable data analysis tool for non-coders. Upload CSV or Excel files, ask in plain English, and it writes and executes real Python code behind the scenes to produce tables, charts, and insights.
pros: Executes actual Python — genuine calculation not text generation
Can clean data, merge files, and export results
Shows the code it ran so you can verify the approach
cons: Files reset after session — re-upload each time

cards.title: Claude (Pro tier)
cards.description: Excellent at reading, discussing, and summarizing data in prose. Strong for interpretation, written narratives of findings, and suggesting analysis approaches. Less focused on code execution than ChatGPT.
pros: Superior prose explanations of data findings
Handles reading very large CSV files in context
Strong at suggesting analysis approaches before executing
cons: Code execution less seamless than ChatGPT

cards.title: Gemini in Google Sheets
cards.description: If your data lives in Google Sheets, Gemini integrates natively in a sidebar. Ask questions about your sheet, get formula recommendations, create charts, and get summaries without leaving Sheets.
pros: Native Sheets integration — data stays in place
Can write and insert formulas directly into cells
cons: Requires a Google AI Pro or Workspace plan
Less powerful for complex multi-step analysis

data.title: Initial data exploration (start here)
data.content:
"I have uploaded a CSV. The columns represent [describe what each column is]. Please:
1. Tell me the dimensions (row and column count)
2. List column names and data types
3. Flag data quality issues: missing values, outliers, inconsistent formats
4. Give me 3-5 initial observations about the data"

data.title: Specific insight request
data.content:
"Using this sales data, answer these questions:
1. Which 5 salespeople had the highest close rates last quarter?
2. Is there a pattern between deal size and sales cycle length?
3. Which product categories are growing vs declining?

For each answer: (a) a brief written finding, (b) a supporting data table or chart"

data.title: Data transformation and export
data.content:
"Clean this dataset:
1. Remove rows where [column] is empty
2. Standardize [column] to Title Case
3. Convert [column] from MM/DD/YYYY to YYYY-MM-DD
4. Add a calculated column: [describe calculation]

After cleaning, give me the updated file to download."

data.text: Tips when using code-execution features (Code Interpreter / Notebooks)

items: Always start with an exploration prompt so the model can infer types and spot issues before transformations.
Ask the model to show the code it will run and explain each step in plain English before executing.
Request intermediate outputs (sample rows, head/tail) to validate transformations incrementally.
Pinpoint heavy operations (joins, group-bys) and ask for estimated runtime or memory usage for large files.
Save both the cleaned dataset and the code snippet for reproducibility and audit.

data.text: AI outputs must be verified. Use deterministic checks (schema validation, numeric equality), spot checks, and independent lookups. For any aggregated number you plan to present, verify the calculation on a sample of rows or in a trusted BI tool.

rows: Compare original and processed row counts
Detect accidental row drops or duplicates
Recompute top 3 aggregates manually or in Excel
Verify date conversions and timezone handling on sample rows
Date errors cause wrong trends and seasonality
Run JSON/CSV schema checks on exported outputs
Prevents malformed outputs from breaking downstream systems
Ask the model to list assumptions and confidence for each finding

data.title: Verify numbers before presenting them
data.text: AI-generated analysis can contain calculation errors, especially on aggregations, date math, and percentages. Always spot-check key numbers against your source data before presenting results to stakeholders. For high-stakes decisions, verify analysis in Excel or a BI tool.
Common issues and how to mitigate them

rows: AI may miscount, misaggregate, or use wrong formulas
Spot-check 3-5 numbers manually against source data
Mixing up date formats, treating text as numbers
Describe your data schema at the start of the session
Very large files may be truncated silently
Check row counts before and after upload
Save all outputs and code before closing the chat
AI may claim correlation where there is none
Ask: 'How confident are you? What might make this wrong?' and run statistical tests

data.text: Advanced patterns: RAG, sampling, and reproducibility

For workflows that require up-to-date or domain-specific knowledge, combine retrieval (RAG) with analysis: retrieve canonical documents or reference tables, condition the model on those passages, then run code-based analysis. For uncertain reasoning, sample multiple analyses and aggregate results (self-consistency). Always save the code and seed values to reproduce results.

data.text: Treat data handling as a first-class design requirement. Redact or tokenize PII, use enterprise plans when connecting production data, and apply least-privilege credentials for any tool that can write or take irreversible actions. Maintain an audit trail of uploads, prompts, and outputs for compliance.

rows: Run PII detector before sending text to model
Separate read-only and write keys; require human sign-off
Choose vendor plans that opt out of training
Use private instances or contractual training opt-out

data.text: Integration patterns: from ad-hoc to production

items: Ad-hoc analysis: manual upload to chat UI, exploratory prompts, download results.
Semi-automated: scheduled jobs that upload CSVs to an analysis agent and email reports for human review.
Automated pipelines: orchestrator calls LLM + code-execution, runs verification, writes results to BI or database with human approval gates.
RAG-backed dashboards: retrieve canonical tables for grounding, run periodic analyses, surface anomalies to analysts.

rows: "I uploaded a file named [filename]. Describe: 1) rows and columns, 2) column types, 3) top 5 data quality issues, 4) 3 initial insights. Keep each section short."
Start every session with this to orient the model
"Using the uploaded data, return the top 10 customers by revenue as a CSV with columns: customer_id, customer_name, revenue. Also include a short paragraph explaining any surprising entries."
"Analyze [date_column] vs [metric_column] for anomalies in the last 12 months. Return a chart and a table of anomaly dates with the metric value and suggested reason (one sentence)."
Ask for both visual and tabular evidence

items: Confirm row counts and key aggregations against source data.
Validate date conversions and timezone assumptions.
Ensure charts have labeled axes and units.
Include a short 'assumptions and limitations' section with each report.
Archive the code and prompt used to generate the analysis for reproducibility.

data.text: AI makes data analysis accessible to non-technical users, but reliability depends on good prompts, verification, and operational discipline. Start with exploration prompts, require supporting tables or charts for every claim, verify key numbers, and save the code and prompts that produced the results. Over time, these practices turn ad-hoc analysis into dependable workflows.

data.title: AI data analysis essentials
points: ChatGPT Plus Code Interpreter: upload CSV or Excel, ask in plain English, get real charts and tables
Gemini: best if your data lives in Google Sheets — native in-app integration
Start every session with an exploration prompt: dimensions, column types, data quality, first observations
Request output in two parts: written finding plus supporting table or chart
Always spot-check key numbers before presenting — AI calculations can have errors
Save code, prompts, and outputs for reproducibility and audit
